design_rationale:
WORKLOG — air_ticketing_desk, task 1 (root problem: carrying a lapsed travel credit forward)
Revision 2. Round 1 closed all seven instantiation gates; the independent policy-task audit then found
two red items bearing on this task (CG-10 and CG-11) and three observations. This revision closes them;
the record is in REVISIONS at the foot.

STEP 0 — DRAW, ASSET LEDGER AND SCOPE CLAIM
  .venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0000_online_travel_agency/tasks/air_ticketing_desk --task 1
  {"task": 1, "key": "online_travel_agency/air_ticketing_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 6]}
Two problems, one prerequisite, six declared factors on each computation — met exactly.
Occupied by task 0 and untouchable here: air_ext_cancellation_penalty, air_ext_airline_tax_return,
air_ext_cancelled_ticket_credit and air_ext_pooled_credit_release with their four tools — everything
about pricing a cancellation, returning taxes, producing a voucher from a cancelled ticket and spending
live credit on a new itinerary. Claimed here: the other half of air_credit_validity, the clause about a
voucher that has already lapsed, through air_ext_credit_reissue_fee and
air_ext_lapsed_credit_carry_forward with charge_credit_reissue_fee_efe635ea and
reissue_lapsed_travel_credit_f544c035. The two scopes are disjoint in policies, tools and write
operations and together cover all six policies. This is the last task of the difficulty.

WHY IT MAKES A GOOD TEST
The caller's request is the plainest thing in the file — she would like to keep a credit that has run out
rather than lose it — and it is the whole of what she knows. The terms then impose one thing she never
mentions: the value carried onto a fresh voucher is fixed only after the reissue fee stands charged on
the booking, and that fee is itself a six-factor figure that more than triples the brand's flat 75.00.
An agent who mints the fresh voucher first, or never charges the fee, writes 1409.59
instead of 1185.59 with nothing in the environment to say so. Beyond the ordering, the two numbers force a
real reconciliation: how many vouchers stand lapsed and what they total, when the most recently issued of
them lapsed, how long ago the cancellation was confirmed, how old the booking is, how many service-fee
lines stand on it, what the club card carries, and how much of the traveller's hotel spending falls inside
a twelve-month window once a spa charge and an older stay are excluded.

THE PROBLEM-TREE CARD
  root: air_ext_lapsed_credit_carry_forward (reissue_lapsed_travel_credit_f544c035, owner=user)
    <- air_ext_credit_reissue_fee (charge_credit_reissue_fee_efe635ea, owner=agent)
One prerequisite problem, exactly the drawn count; one edge, value_input, meeting the floor of
max(n-1,1)=1.
Edge — carry-forward <- reissue fee. gate: the compute binding reissue_fee_charged; form state;
sentence, verbatim in the carry-forward policy's own rule: "The value carried onto the fresh voucher is
fixed only after the reissue fee owed under the fare brand that produced the lapsed voucher stands as a
charged line on the booking."
  Four-point test: (1) the connective is "only after"; (2) what it waits on is a record-visible state, a
  charged reissue fee line standing on the booking, in the words the ledger uses; (3) no tool, policy id,
  snake_case token or row id; (4) a hard requirement, scoped exactly to the reissue fee of the brand that
  produced the lapsed voucher. Exactly one write of this difficulty charges an air_fare_charge line with
  charge_category credit_reissue_fee, and the fee policy's own rule says in its own terms that its result
  is that fee. Derivation: the sentence says the value carried waits on a charged reissue fee line; the
  records show nine lines — six fare, tax and service lines, a cancellation penalty and two credit issues
  — and none of them a reissue fee; the fee policy is the only rule whose result is a reissue fee charged
  on a booking; so the fee is charged first. One reading.
  Seed evidence that it is false at the opening: every charge_category on the booking is
  agency_service_fee, base_fare, taxes_and_carrier_fees, cancellation_penalty or credit_issue, and
  air_bookings.a15cde5e-e2b3-451a-b835-8d74e25bdae9.amount_paid_usd is 3473.90, exactly the six charge lines plus the penalty with nothing
  added for a reissue.
The state form carried the edge, so no fallback_reason. Topological order: the fee, then the
carry-forward; no parallel edges. Deletion sensitivity, from the verification run: skipping the fee moves
the scored value of the carry-forward 1185.59 to 1409.59.
user_scenario mentions no prerequisite problem; the tool layer validates none.

THE BASE-INVARIANT CARD
air_fare_charge (step 9): governed by air_service_fee, air_club_benefit_interaction and
air_biz_exclusion, none of which states a structured gate for that subject, so each is inherited whole
and recorded as policy_scope, and each was checked in prose: the service-fee rule's own subject is the fee
charged at ticketing, which this booking carries twice, and its currency-markup clause is not engaged
because the fee is taken in US dollars; the club-benefit rule's waivers attach to the tier held at ticket
issue and cover the agency service fee and the first checked bag, and the relief this policy gives on the
reissue fee is now declared against it by name; the corporate exclusion does not bite because
corporate_program_id is empty, so consumer terms apply in full.
air_credit_issue (step 11): governed by air_credit_validity, gate cancelled_before_issue — "A voucher is
issued only while the booking record stands at cancelled, refund pending or refunded" — satisfied because
the booking stands at refunded. The brand's credit validity term is 12 months and not zero; the once-only
reissue limit is respected because no reissue line stands on this booking.
There is no time eligibility gate on either write, so temporal_feasibility is empty. That is not an
oversight: the only time gate in this area, credit_still_valid, governs air_credit_redeem, and nothing is
redeemed here. The lapse is not a gate — a lapsed voucher may be reissued, which is the clause this task
claims — but it is now tested in the compute rather than merely asserted in prose: the vouchers standing
on the booking are taken as one set, the set stands lapsed when the voucher most recently issued on it has
lapsed, and where it has not, nothing is owed and nothing is carried.

THE BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD
Target of both writes: the ORD-CDG Economy Saver booking standing at refunded (locator HF3D8K), the only
air booking on the profile and the one the caller reads out of her diary. Correlation key:
air_bookings.air_booking_id. The narrower source object both writes carry is the issue line of the largest
lapsed voucher, 1900.00, written into source_event_id — not the booking reference alone, and not the
smaller voucher. Excluded by the rules rather than by convenience: the 520.00 spa charge on the Lisbon
folio (an incidental, not a room charge), the two 410.00 room charges of May 2025 (outside the
twelve-month window) and the qualifying points rows (the relief factor reads the spendable balance).

THE FACTOR CARD
air_ext_credit_reissue_fee (6 factors; whole baseline 75.0, gold 224.0)
  lapse_clock_anchor (method, multi-source): non-transferable credits and more than one lapsed voucher ->
    the clock runs from the day the cancellation was confirmed; transferable and more than one -> from the
    day the most recent voucher was issued; otherwise -> from the day the most recent voucher lapsed.
    Three different anchor dates from three different places. Evidence: Economy Saver credits are
    non-transferable and two vouchers stand lapsed -> 2024-11-05, giving 22 months.
    Baseline -> 187.25.
  lapse_age_loading (parameter): longer than 12 months -> 1.60; longer than 3 but not 12 -> 1.25;
    otherwise as it stands. Evidence: 22 months -> 1.60. Baseline -> 161.0.
  voucher_count_basis (method): two or more lapsed vouchers -> the fee once for each; a single lapsed
    voucher on a transferable brand -> once and half again; otherwise once. Evidence: two vouchers -> 2.
    Baseline -> 140.0.
  standing_value_loading (parameter): at or above 2500.00 -> 60.00; at or above 800.00 -> 25.00;
    otherwise nothing. Evidence: 1900.00 + 1216.00 = 3116.00 -> 60.00.
    Baseline -> 182.0.
  booking_age_surcharge (parameter): opened longer ago than 36 months -> 45.00; longer than 18 but not 36
    -> 20.00; otherwise nothing. Evidence: booked 2024-06-18, 26 months -> 20.00.
    Baseline -> 210.0.
  member_fee_relief (parameter, cross-difficulty club, multi-source): senior tiers with 20,000 points or
    more -> 0.50; Blue/Silver/Gold with 20,000 or more -> 0.30; any active tier with fewer -> 0.10;
    otherwise nothing. Evidence: club_memberships bbba1023-ffd0-4e22-8053-8ec915daeb14, active Wanderlane Silver, 26,400 spendable
    points -> 0.30. Baseline -> 320.0.
air_ext_lapsed_credit_carry_forward (6 factors; whole baseline 1676.0, gold 1185.59)
  lapsed_set_selection (method, multi-source): two or more lapsed vouchers whose most recently issued one
    lapsed longer ago than 6 months -> the total of the lapsed vouchers issued within the retention window;
    two or more whose most recent lapsed within 6 months -> the total of every lapsed voucher whatever its
    age; otherwise the largest lapsed voucher. Three different aggregates over three different row sets, and
    no fee term in any of them. Evidence: the later voucher lapsed 2026-01-10, 8 months back, and both
    vouchers were issued 21 and 20 whole months ago, inside the 24-month retention window -> 3116.00.
    Baseline the largest alone -> 623.8. Every voucher the fee was charged for is carried forward, and the
    fee itself is deducted once and only at the end.
  staleness_carry_share (parameter): cancellation confirmed longer ago than 12 months -> 0.70; longer than
    6 but not 12 -> 0.85; otherwise in full. Evidence: 2024-11-05, 22 months -> 0.70.
    Baseline -> 1802.56.
  lead_traveller_share (parameter, multi-source): non-transferable credits and three or more fare lines ->
    0.40; non-transferable and exactly two -> 0.60; otherwise in full. Evidence: two base-fare lines on a
    non-transferable brand -> 0.60. Baseline -> 2145.32. The value it acts on is
    the party's whole standing value, both travellers' vouchers included, so the ground it states — that
    the fresh voucher stands in the lead traveller's name alone — is not one the world has already
    satisfied before the factor is reached.
  card_carry_uplift (parameter, cross-difficulty club, multi-source): senior tiers enrolled at or beyond
    60 months -> 0.10; Blue/Silver/Gold at or beyond -> 0.06; any active tier within -> 0.02; otherwise
    nothing. Evidence: the Silver card enrolled 2019-08-22, 84 months -> 0.06.
    Baseline -> 1107.07.
  house_activity_uplift (parameter, cross-difficulty stay, multi-source): room charges of the last twelve
    months at or above 1500.00 with an active card -> 0.08; above nothing but below 1500.00 with a card ->
    0.04; above nothing with no card -> 0.02; otherwise nothing. Evidence: four room nights of 348.00,
    1392.00 in the window -> 0.04. Baseline -> 1133.24. Near-misses: the 520.00
    spa charge on the same folio would take the total to 1912.00, and the two 410.00 room charges of May
    2025 to 2212.00, either of which would move the tier to 0.08.
  service_fee_recovery (parameter, multi-source): two or more service-fee lines on a brand whose fee is at
    or above 25.00 -> 30.00 off; exactly one such line -> 15.00 off; otherwise nothing. Evidence: two
    service-fee lines and an Economy Saver fee of 29.95 -> 30.00. Baseline -> 1215.59.
Counts: 6 + 6, exactly the drawn multiset; four parameter and two method on the fee, five parameter and
one method on the carry-forward; each method factor's tiers read different anchors or different row sets
rather than substituting a coefficient. Seven multi-source factors and three cross-difficulty factors
(two club, one stay). No factor's tier is read off a field naming its own outcome.

WHAT EACH CLASS OF SEED ROW IS FOR
The booking supplies the fare brand (the reissue fee, the credit validity term, the transferability and
the agency service fee), the day it was opened (the age surcharge) and the moment the cancellation was
confirmed (the lapse anchor and the staleness carry). The six fare, tax and service lines supply the two
base-fare lines the lead-traveller share counts and the two service-fee lines the recovery counts, and
with the penalty they make the paid total and the credit balance add up. The cancellation penalty is what
makes the two vouchers total 3116.00 rather than 3324.90. The two vouchers do four jobs: their count
drives the fee multiple, their total drives the value loading, the later one's expiry decides both the
lapsed-set tier and whether the set stands lapsed at all, and both are carried forward. The club card
decides two factors; its five points rows are the ledger the spendable balance is read from and are pulled
into the closure by a read node. The two hotel stays and their seven folio lines decide the house uplift
and carry both of its near-misses.
Automatic clauses: nothing accrues daily on an air booking, nothing locks at a threshold, and the only
maturity in play is the credit validity term, which has already run on both vouchers — the premise of the
task. The booking stands at refunded, a terminal state.
Cache design: no stale cache. amount_paid_usd and credit_balance_usd both agree with the ledger at the
opening and neither is read by any formula.

THE PERSONA
Rashida is the opposite of task 0's caller in every dimension that matters: older, slower, discursive
where Priya is clipped, apologetic about rambling where Priya is faintly impatient, volunteering a little
harmless colour where Priya volunteers nothing. She gives her name unprompted and everything else only
when asked, and reads her mobile out twice. Her two cannot-answer branches are explicit: she does not know
her membership number and would have to look for the card, and she has never kept the trip's numbers
straight and would rather the desk told her — which closes the only route by which she could leak a
computed figure. Her re-check reaction is the flat "that does not sound like the sort of number I was
expecting". The prerequisite reaches her only as a reaction: if the agent says something must be put
through first she says that is fine and asks them to get on with it, explicitly without asking what it is
or how much. Her closing reaction answers the last gold action and stops.

REACHABILITY IN ONE CONVERSATION
Name and mobile; find_customers resolves the profile; two details match at verification.
find_air_bookings returns the one booking with its brand, dates and balances. find_air_booking_events
returns the nine lines: the fare, tax and service lines the party and service factors count, the penalty
that explains the voucher total, and the two vouchers with their values, codes and expiry dates.
find_club_memberships returns the card and find_club_points_entries the movements its balance stands on;
find_stay_reservations and find_stay_folio_entries return the two stays and the seven folio lines the
house uplift is reconciled from. Then one agent write and one hand-over. The only identifier not read from
a lookup is the fresh voucher code, which the reissue tool mints and returns in its own confirmation.
Nothing waits on anything outside the conversation; the whole run is under one frozen_time of
2026-09-17 14:05:00 CDT.

TWO-WAY EQUIVALENCE OF RULE AND COMPUTE
Both computations state how their own result assembles, in the rule and the baseline alike. The fee is
settled in two named stages — the tariff component, which is the brand's credit reissue fee taken at
whatever loading the unclaimed time earns and then taken as many times as the fee falls due, and the fee
charged, which is that component with anything added in dollars added once for the booking and never once
for each voucher, and any relief then taken as a share of the whole. The carry-forward names the value
standing, says that every share and every uplift bears on it, and says that anything taken off in dollars
— the reissue fee above all — is taken off last of all, after every share and every uplift. Both carry the
same composition convention as the other four computations: shares act one after another and never combine
into a single rate, while uplifts combine into a single uplift applied once. Every factor sentence names
the stage its outcome enters, by the baseline's own name for it.
Forward: every binding that reads the world or makes a choice carries a verbatim quotation — the two
voucher aggregates and the maximum, the two LATEST reads, all four month spans, the lapsed-set test, the
two cross-category reads on the club card, the XSUM over the hotel folios, every ladder, both floors and
both roundings. Reverse: every load-bearing sentence of both rules lands on a binding — "taken once for
the voucher" on the fee multiple's fall-through, "in whole calendar months" on the MONTHS calls, "over the
last twelve months" on the within_months=12 filter of the folio sum, "room charges" on the event_type
filter that excludes the spa line, the lapsed-set sentence on set_lapsed, "never below zero" on the MX
guards and each rounding sentence on the single RND in each result. verify_quotes.py re-runs both sweeps
mechanically.
Declared overrides: both policies name air_credit_validity's "A voucher that has lapsed may be reissued
once onto a fresh voucher against the brand's reissue fee", one refining what the reissue costs and one
what survives onto the fresh voucher; and the fee policy additionally names
air_club_benefit_interaction's "the club tier held on the day the ticket is issued decides whether the
agency service fee is waived and whether the first checked bag is carried free", replaced by the governing
sentence of its own club relief. The rest of air_credit_validity stands: the once-only limit, the fresh
voucher's validity term counted from the day of reissue, the name it is issued in, and the bar on paying a
voucher out in money.

THE STANDARD SOLUTION
Locate and verify. Read the booking: an Economy Saver ticket at refunded with two travel credits whose
expiry dates have both passed, so the set stands lapsed. Read the club card and its ledger, and the hotel
stays and their folios. From the terms: the value carried waits on a charged reissue fee, so the fee comes
first. The fee: 75.00 at the long-lapse loading 1.60 because the clock runs 22 months from the
cancellation date on a non-transferable multi-voucher booking, taken twice because two vouchers stand
lapsed, giving 240.00; plus 60.00 for a standing value of 3116.00 and 20.00 for a booking 26 months old,
giving 320.00; less the 30 per cent relief a Silver card with 26,400 points earns -> 224.0. Then hand the
reissue to the traveller. The value carried: both vouchers, 3116.00, both issued inside the 24-month
retention window and neither of them reduced by any part of the reissue fee at this point; at the long-stale
carry 0.70 and the paired-lead share 0.60, giving 1308.72; uplifted by 6 per cent for the card and 4 per
cent for 1392.00 of room charges in the window, giving 1439.592; less 30.00 of service recovery and the
224.0 fee, met once, -> 1185.59, on a fresh voucher running to 2027-09-17.

THE PLACES A CARELESS AGENT GOES WRONG
Reissuing first and charging the fee afterwards, or not at all — the carry-forward rule says the value is
fixed only after the fee stands charged, and the figures differ by 224.0. Counting the lapse from the
voucher expiry rather than the cancellation date and taking the 1.25 loading — settled by the brand's
transferability and the voucher count. Carrying only the largest voucher forward though the fee was
charged for both — the first tier of the lapsed-set rule carries every one of them that was issued inside
the retention window, and deducts no part of the fee, which is met once at the end. Adding the spa charge or the May 2025 room nights to the twelve-month room
total — excluded by the event the rule names and the window it states. Reading the club relief off the
qualifying points rather than the spendable balance — the rule names the spendable points. Charging the
fee once rather than once per voucher — settled by the count.

VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN
Verification harness actually run (a throwaway harness, deliberately outside the artifact tree; what each part does is stated here so it can be rebuilt from this dossier alone): solve.py recomputes every value at its handling time, substitutes each factor's baseline and then all of them at once, and replays each edge with the depended-on write skipped; run1.py drives it for this task; figs.py dumps the verified figures so no proof field is typed by hand; verify_quotes.py checks every compute_basis quotation, ladder phrase and baseline sentence verbatim against its own rule; verify_figs.py reads every figure a proof field asserts back against the recomputation and fails on any mismatch.
Output of run1.py:
  air_ext_credit_reissue_fee          expected=224.0   baseline=75.0
    lapse_clock_anchor 187.25 | lapse_age_loading 161.0 | voucher_count_basis 140.0 | standing_value_loading 182.0 | booking_age_surcharge 210.0 | member_fee_relief 320.0
  air_ext_lapsed_credit_carry_forward expected=1185.59  baseline=1676.0
    lapsed_set_selection 623.8 | staleness_carry_share 1802.56 | lead_traveller_share 2145.32 | card_carry_uplift 1107.07 | house_activity_uplift 1133.24 | service_fee_recovery 1215.59
  prereq sensitivity: the carry-forward with and without the fee, 1185.59 to 1409.59
These figures are exactly the computations and the gold arguments on disk, and verify_figs.py enforces it.
Gates: check_extended EXTENDED OK; check_task_tools TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; replay_tasks REPLAY OK;
check_solvability SOLVABILITY OK; check_compute COMPUTE OK; check_grounding GROUNDING OK;
check_cross_fire SCOPE OK.

CLOSURE
  air_ext_credit_reissue_fee -> charge_credit_reissue_fee_efe635ea -> step 9
    reissue_fee_usd 224.0 -> a reissue fee line standing charged on the Paris booking
  air_ext_lapsed_credit_carry_forward -> reissue_lapsed_travel_credit_f544c035 -> step 11
    carried_value_usd 1185.59 -> a fresh voucher standing open in her name to 2027-09-17
charter_scope, required_documents and computations name exactly those two policies in that order, and
charter_scope.task_tools names exactly those two tools in order of first call.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT
With the hidden assets masked and working only from the policy prose that will be published, the tool
schemas, the rows the share tools return and the persona's lines: the caller wants a lapsed credit kept;
the carry-forward rule says its value is fixed only after a reissue fee stands charged; no such line
stands; so the fee is charged first and is itself priced from the lapse clock, the voucher count, the
standing value, the booking's age and the club card. Working both figures by hand from the prose gave
224.0 and 1185.59, the same as gold, with no second reading of the object, the order or any parameter.

REVISIONS
R2.1 (audit CG-10 / F1-1) Symptom: voucher_count_basis charged the fee once for each of two lapsed
  vouchers while lapsed_set_selection carried only the largest forward, so 1216.00 of the traveller's own
  credit was extinguished by the very transaction she paid for — not an outcome a travel business
  publishes. Root cause: the two policies of one tree counted different numbers of vouchers as being put
  back into use. Change: lapsed_set_selection's first tier now carries the total of every lapsed voucher,
  less the brand's credit reissue fee for each voucher beyond the first, so what the fee is charged for is
  what comes back; the other two tiers keep the plain total and the largest alone, so the factor still
  selects three different row sets and remains an honest method. Re-run: the carried value moves from
  623.80 to 1185.59 and the second voucher's value survives.
R2.2 (audit CG-11 / F1-2) Symptom: lead_traveller_share took a further share off a value from which the
  other traveller's voucher had already been removed, on the stated ground that the fresh voucher stands
  in the lead traveller's name alone — a ground already satisfied before the factor applied. Root cause:
  the tier's condition is stated of the booking while the quantity it acted on was no longer the booking's.
  Change: fixed by R2.1 — value_standing is now the party's whole standing value, both travellers'
  vouchers included, so the share reduces a party-wide figure to the lead traveller's own for the first
  and only time. Re-run: the factor still bears weight (baseline 2145.32) and its
  stated ground now matches what it acts on.
R2.3 (audit CG-5 / F1-4) Symptom: both policies spoke throughout of vouchers "standing lapsed" while their
  computes counted every credit issue row with no test against credit_expires_on, so a live voucher would
  be counted as lapsed and a second handling of this booking would count the fresh voucher among them.
  Change: both rules now state that the vouchers standing on the booking are taken as one set, that the set
  stands lapsed when the voucher most recently issued on it has lapsed, and that where it has not the set
  is still redeemable and nothing is owed; both computes carry a set_lapsed binding that tests exactly that
  and zeroes the result otherwise. Re-run: on this world the test passes and the scored values are
  unchanged, and the prose and the compute now say the same thing.
R2.4 (audit F1-3) Symptom: member_fee_relief reduced the fee on the strength of a club tier although base
  air_club_benefit_interaction, cited in base_policy_refs, says the tier decides only the agency service fee
  waiver and the free first bag, with no overwrite naming it. Change: the override is now declared, quoting
  that base sentence and replacing it with the governing sentence of the relief paragraph.
R2.5 (audit F1-5) Symptom: the first tier of lapse_clock_anchor measured "the time the value has stood
  lapsed" from the cancellation date, so roughly fourteen of the twenty-two months counted were months in
  which the value was live. The convention is defensible; the name was not. Change: the quantity is now
  named for what it measures — how long the credit has stood unclaimed — in the rule, the ladder and the
  basis. No figure changes.
R2.6 (audit CG-13) Symptom: the tool docstrings required the amount "already rounded half away from zero to
  the cent" while the runtime rounds half to even. Change: the claim was removed from all six parameter
  descriptions.
R2.7 (audit F0-1, applied difficulty-wide) Change: every proof figure in both task files is now emitted
  from the verification run through figs.py and read back by verify_figs.py, which fails on any mismatch
  between a figure a proof field asserts and the recomputation.

R3.1 (audit CG-16 / F1-6) Symptom: the brand's reissue fee was recovered twice for every voucher beyond
  the first — once by voucher_count_basis on the fee line (84.00 of the 224.00 charged was the second
  voucher's share) and again by the per-voucher deduction the CG-10 remedy had put inside value_standing,
  on top of the baseline's single deduction of the whole charged fee at the end. Root cause: the remedy for
  CG-10 paid for the extra vouchers it started carrying with a term the fee policy had already charged for.
  Change: the per-voucher term is gone from value_standing entirely. The tier keeps a distinct method — the
  total of the lapsed vouchers issued inside the retention window, against the plain total on the second
  tier and the largest alone on the fall-through — so the ladder still selects three different aggregates
  over three different row sets, every lapsed voucher is still carried forward (CG-10 stays closed) and the
  quantity the lead-traveller share acts on is still party-wide (CG-11 stays closed). The three places the
  fee could be recovered were then checked against one another, which is what round 2 failed to do: policy
  air_ext_credit_reissue_fee computes it once per voucher; the carry-forward's selection contains no fee
  term at all; the baseline deducts the charged fee exactly once, and its rule now says so outright — "The
  reissue fee is met once, out of the value being carried forward, and is never taken a second time out of
  the vouchers it was charged for." The fee tool's docstring was corrected in step, since it had described
  the fee as taken from the card as well. Re-run: carried_value_usd moves from 1150.94 to 1185.59, which is
  exactly the counter-figure the audit computed, and every factor still bears weight.
R3.2 (audit CG-15) Symptom: air_ext_lapsed_credit_carry_forward.params.recent_set_share was registered and
  referenced by nothing, a leftover of the tier the CG-10 remedy replaced. Change: removed, and
  retention_window_months added in its place, referenced by the new windowed aggregate.

R4.1 (KB audit R1-1) Symptom: a reader of the published documents built "the credit reissue fee" up from
  the tariff, the loading and both flat additions and then took the whole of it once per voucher, reaching
  280.00 where gold said 224.00. Both readings were faithful to every sentence the corpus carried. Root
  cause: three factor sentences each operated on a quantity all of them called "the credit reissue fee",
  and nothing said which of them binds first. Here the compute was right and the rule was under-specified,
  so the rule moved, not the compute: the fee is now settled in two named stages, the per-voucher multiple
  binds on the tariff component alone, and the two flat amounts are stated as added to the fee charged
  once for the booking and never once for each voucher. Re-run: 224.00, unchanged.
R4.2 (KB audit R1-2, part a) Symptom: the baseline sentence defined the value carried as the largest
  lapsed credit "less the reissue fee charged on the booking", so a reader formed that difference first
  and applied the shares to it, while the compute applies the shares to the value standing and deducts the
  fee last. Root cause: the baseline put the deduction in the wrong place in its own definition. The
  compute was right and the baseline sentence moved: the value standing is now named as a stage in its own
  right, and the deduction is stated as taken off last of all, after every share and every uplift.
  Re-run: 1185.59, unchanged.
R4.3 (KB audit R1-2, part b) Symptom: this policy summed its two uplifts while the sibling voucher policy
  compounded its uplift with its offset, from wording indistinguishable across the four factor documents.
  Change: one convention, stated identically in all six computations — shares act one after another and
  are never combined into a single rate; uplifts are combined into a single uplift and the figure is
  increased once by that total. It reproduces both policies' computes exactly, so the two are no longer
  two conventions but one, and neither scored value moved.
user_scenario:
Rashida Abernathy is sixty-five, a retired school principal in Oak Park who still keeps a diary in pencil. She telephones on a quiet weekday afternoon and talks the way she used to talk to parents: unhurried, circling round to the point, apologising once or twice for rambling. She is not in any hurry and says so.

The point, when she gets to it, is the Paris trip she and her sister never took. It was called off a long while back — she is vague about exactly when and says the desk will have it written down somewhere — and she was given credit for it. She looked at it on her phone over the weekend and it says the credit has run out, which she had not expected and is a little sad about. She says it plainly: "I'd like to hang on to the credit from the Paris trip rather than lose it." She is not asking for money back and says so if the agent raises it; she just wants to be able to use it on a flight later. She is content for the desk to do whatever it must on its side, and she will do whatever part of it is properly hers, but she wants it finished on this call because she does not care for being told to ring back.

She gives her name without prompting. If the desk needs to find her she reads out her mobile, 3122560934, slowly and twice. Asked for something more to prove it is her, she offers the last four of her passport, 1157, and if a third thing is needed she gives her date of birth, 1961-05-09. She mentions in passing that she has been with Wanderlane since long before any of this, but she does not know her membership number and would have to go and look for the card.

She has the old booking reference written in her diary and reads it out when asked: HF3D8K. She has no idea what the trip cost or what the credit is worth — she says her sister paid part of it and she has never been able to keep the numbers straight — and if pressed she says she would rather the desk told her than have her guess. When she is told a figure she accepts it; if a figure sounds a long way off what she half remembers she says only that it does not sound like the sort of number she was expecting and asks whether they could check it against the booking.

If the agent explains that there is something the desk has to put through on the booking before the value can be settled, she says that is fine and asks them to do whatever is needed; she does not ask what it is or how much, and she does not offer a suggestion of her own. When the agent says the value is ready and hands her the step that is hers to do, she says "oh, I see — yes, let me press it then" and runs it, and she will read out what appears on her screen if she is asked. Once she hears that the credit is open again and good for another year, she is content, says that is a weight off, thanks the agent warmly and says goodbye.

The lapse loading: 22 months is longer than the 12-month long-lapse term, so the long-lapse loading 1.60 applies and the fee becomes 120.00. The voucher count basis: two vouchers stand lapsed, so the fee is taken once for each, giving 240.00. The value loading: the two vouchers stand together at 1900.00 + 1216.00 = 3116.00, at or above the 2500.00 high-value band, so 60.00 is added. The booking age surcharge: the booking was opened 2024-06-18, 26 whole calendar months before the handling date, longer ago than the 18-month older-booking term but not longer ago than the 36-month archived-booking term, so 20.00 is added, giving 320.00. The member relief: the traveller holds an active Wanderlane Silver card with 26,400 spendable points standing on it, at or above the 20,000 points band, so the member-fee relief 0.30 applies: 320.00 x 0.70 = 224.00. Two vouchers stand lapsed and that most recent one lapsed 8 whole calendar months before the handling date, longer ago than the 6-month long-lapse term, so the value standing is the total of the lapsed vouchers issued within the 24-month retention window — both of them, posted 2024-11-20 and 2025-01-10, 21 and 20 whole calendar months before the handling date — that is 1900.00 + 1216.00 = 3116.00. The staleness carry: the cancellation was confirmed 2024-11-05, 22 whole calendar months ago, longer ago than the 12-month long-stale term, so the long-stale carry 0.70 applies, giving 2181.20. The lead-traveller share: Economy Saver makes credits non-transferable and exactly two base-fare lines stand on the booking, so the paired-lead share 0.60 applies, giving 1308.72. The card uplift: the traveller holds an active Wanderlane Silver card enrolled 2019-08-22, 84 whole months before the handling date and so at or beyond the 60-month long-membership term, so 0.06 is added. The house uplift: room charges posted to her hotel stays in the last twelve months total 4 x 348.00 = 1392.00 (the 520.00 spa charge of 2026-03-17 is not a room charge, and the 2 x 410.00 room charges of May 2025 fall outside the window), which is above nothing but below the 1500.00 house-spend band, and an active card stands on the profile, so 0.04 is added: 1308.72 x 1.10 = 1439.592. The service recovery: two agency service fee lines stand on the booking and the Economy Saver agency service fee of 29.95 is at or above the 25.00 service-fee band, so 30.00 is taken off. The reissue fee charged on the booking, 224.00, is met out of the value once: 1439.592 - 30.00 - 224.00 = 1185.592. Rounded to two decimal places: 1185.59.

Not one of them is a reissue fee, so the reissue fee charged on the booking is nil; the booking's paid total of 3473.90 is exactly the sum of its six charge lines and the penalty, with nothing added for a reissue.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Once the fee write lands, a reissue fee line of 224.00 stands charged on the booking and the reissue_fee_charged binding of the carry-forward computation takes 224.00 instead of 0.00, met once out of the value carried.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree has a single prerequisite and therefore a single order: the fee is charged, then the value is carried forward. There are no parallel edges to reorder. The order is not a matter of convention either: the carry-forward rule states outright that its result is fixed only after the reissue fee stands as a charged line, and skipping the fee changes the scored value, so the two writes do not commute and no second terminal state exists.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the reissue-fee write and replaying everything else moves the scored value of air_ext_lapsed_credit_carry_forward from 1185.59 to 1409.59. The figure is the recomputation itself, not one carried forward from another step.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The persona raises one thing: that she would like to hang on to the credit from the Paris trip rather than lose it. It nowhere mentions a fee, a charge or anything that has to be put through first, and nowhere asks whether something is outstanding. Her only line touching the prerequisite is the passive one that follows the agent raising it — she says that is fine, asks them to do whatever is needed, and explicitly does not ask what it is or how much.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: Neither task tool validates the prerequisite. reissue_lapsed_travel_credit_f544c035 looks up the booking only to copy its customer reference onto the fresh line and then calls ctx.create unconditionally; it never looks for a reissue fee line, refuses nothing and hints at nothing, and would mint a fresh voucher of whatever value it is given on the opening world just as faithfully. charge_credit_reissue_fee_efe635ea likewise posts its line without inspecting anything about the vouchers. The whole consequence of skipping the fee falls on the terminal hash.
